title: Cold rebuild: Scale a StatefulSet
summary: Rebuild Scale a StatefulSet from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Scale a StatefulSet** in *Jobs, CronJobs, DaemonSets, StatefulSets*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: StatefulSet scale-down order. What does this print?
code: for (int i = from - 1; i >= to; i--)
steps.explain: Highest ordinal first. Scaling up creates `db-2`, `db-3` again in ascending order and reattaches their old PVCs.

steps.title: Rebuild Scale a StatefulSet cold
prompt: Write `List<string> Scale(string name, int from, int to)` returning the actions a StatefulSet controller takes, one pod at a time:

- scale up: `"create name-i"` for each new ordinal in **ascending** order, plus `"create pvc data-name-i"` **before** each pod, but only if that ordinal never existed before (in this exercise, ordinals below `from` existed; ordinals at or above `from` never did)
- scale down: `"delete name-i"` in **descending** order (PVCs are kept, so no PVC actions)
`Scale("db", 1, 3)` returns `["create pvc data-db-1", "create db-1", "create pvc data-db-2", "create db-2"]`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<string> Scale(string name, int from, int to)
